rule_under_audit: Trusted decisive failure => REJECT, even when other evidence (the mismatched acceptance artifact) is invalid.

sufficiency_conclusion.argument: 1) Origin: the probe is a fixed, reviewable script derived from the issue report (probes.py), not from the candidate or its claimed test results. 2) Execution linkage: run via subprocess on a clean base checkout and again only after the exact reviewed candidate patch (sha recorded) is applied; pre fails with the reported NotImplementedError, post still fails. The same patch sha binds both executions to the review target. 3) Decisiveness for the benchmark decision: the directed pair symptom-present-before / symptom-still-present-after is a direct counterexample to the author positive claim and the server strict policy labels it `contradicted` from this channel alone. Under the frozen three-state rule this is a trusted decisive failure => REJECT independently of the unlinked acceptance artifact.

scope_limits_must_be_reported_in_paper: The probe is a LOCAL, issue-text-derived reproduction script, NOT the maintainer FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS suite. builder.py applies the official test_patch only afterwards (line 233+), so the symptom verdict is not an acceptance verdict.

merge_acceptable (builder.py:274) is defined by maintainer F2P and regressed-P2P tests; symptom_persists=true does NOT by itself prove the maintainer suite fails. A patch can silence an ad-hoc probe yet fail tests, or vice versa.

The post run changes exception type (NotImplementedError -> TypeError): this strengthens "symptom not fixed" but the probe is a single assertion surface; local/environment anomalies are possible (mitigated: baseline also run in the same environment, python 3.11.15 recorded, so a pure environment failure would need to produce DIFFERENT errors pre/post).

One instance (sympy-18211) is decisive in this fixture set; the general claim "trusted failure => REJECT" is validated across only a small issue cluster and must not be presented as a general merge-acceptability theorem.

Independence is structural (separate channel, strict policy never reads acceptance outcomes), but both channels share the same review session and candidate tree; they are independent as EVIDENCE SOURCES, not as physical executions.
implication_for_h1_h3: Because this REJECT-grade failure is available to the reviewer in T3D-Strict/T3D-Escalate/T3A-T, NEED_EVIDENCE there on linkage=false grounds is pre-registered Over-Abstention (H1) and a Verification-Decision Gap (H3): the reviewer let an invalid ORTHOGONAL channel cancel a valid decisive one.
